en.title: Minimum Range Operations to Cover Zero Runs
en.description:
Each operation chooses exactly k consecutive positions and sets them all to 1. Find the minimum number of operations so that the string no longer contains m consecutive 0s. Existing 1s are unaffected.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m k, and the second line contains the binary string. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤m,k≤n.
en.explanation: The examples give 1, 0 and 3 respectively. In the first example, setting positions 3 to 4 to 1 gives 001100.
hints: Accumulate the zero run from left to right; the first time m 0s have accumulated, place the length-k interval covering that position as far right as possible and set it to 1, skip that interval, and reset the zero count.
